title: When the Smile Sings
premise: Quentin Dravenmoor, a pest controller with a hard rule against believing in anything without a Latin name, is called to Hollowmere House where something in the walls leaves fingerprints at the height of a child's shoulder. The house's surviving owner, Elowen, has spent thirty years recording her own sleep because the house sings to her at night — and when Quentin's equipment captures a second voice answering her questions in her own cadence, they realize the song is a summons with verses, and the last verse has never been sung aloud. As the frost creeps inward and the fingerprints climb higher each night, Quentin must choose between duty to the living client and love for a woman who may already be half-claimed. In the end, Elowen sings the final verse alone to bind the thing back into the walls, and Quentin — who still refuses to believe — survives by carrying the melody out of the house in his head, where it hums whenever he sleeps.
about_author: L. M. Amberdale is the pen name of a former night-shift archivist who catalogued estate recordings from country houses across northern England. They write horror that insists the most frightening documents are the ones that were never meant to be heard.

chapters.title: Fingerprints at Shoulder Height
chapters.summary: Quentin Dravenmoor, POV. Called to Hollowmere House for 'rodents,' Quentin finds no droppings, no gnawing — only small fingerprints in the dust, too many joints per finger, climbing the staircase wall. The client, Elowen Vasse, is calm to the point of wrongness and asks him to stay the night. Emotional beat: professional skepticism curdling into unease as the evidence refuses every rational category.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Alternating Quentin and Elowen POVs. Overnight, Quentin's monitoring equipment records Elowen's sleep-talk — and a second voice answering her questions, using her intonations, in a language that predates the house. Elowen confesses the recordings span thirty years and the voice is getting closer to the microphone. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in shared terror, as two strangers become co-conspirators against the house.

chapters.title: The Verse That Waits
chapters.summary: Elowen's POV, with Quentin's interludes. Elowen reveals the song has verses and that her mother sang three of them before the frost took her; the last verse, sung by the right voice, either banishes the thing or completes it. The fingerprints reach the height of Quentin's head, and frost patterns spell the melody's notation on the windows. Emotional beat: love against duty — Elowen tries to send Quentin away, and he refuses to leave.

chapters.title: Before the Frost Writes Its Final Pattern
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs converging on one night. The thing comes down from the walls wearing Elowen's mother's voice, and Quentin must hold the melody in his head without singing while Elowen performs the last verse, trading her voice for the house's silence. She survives, hollowed and whisper-voiced. Emotional beat: the price of survival — Quentin leaves still not believing, humming a song he never learned.
